days.label: Monday
days.text: Monday has a real show to start the week. LA indie rockers Cheekface with Apes of the State ($30) play the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge, doors at 7 and music at 7:30. Film people get a good one at Partizanfilm on College Street, where directors Avalon Fast and Jillian Frank bring their new indie feature Drinking and Driving for an 8:05 screening and stick around for a conversation after. Language lovers have Spanish Chat Mondays at Three Needs from 7 to 8, beginners and native speakers both welcome, and pickup dodgeball runs at the Miller Center from 7 to 8:15, $5 a game with teams drawn at random. Mountain bikers can join the Novice Monday guided ride at Catamount in Williston, meeting at 6 for a mellow hour and a half on beginner friendly trails, free for members with a $10.70 day membership for everyone else. Monday Night Bingo at the Elks Lodge on North Avenue goes from 4:30 to 9:30 with $100 regular game payouts and a $1,000 jackpot.

days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday is the last day of the Humane Society of Chittenden County's Adopt-A-Thon , with adoption fees waived for every pet 6 months and older, and the South Burlington shelter is open from 1 to 5. Movie night is free, since Main Street Landing screens Kubrick's Barry Lyndon at the Film House at 7, first come first served, with donations at the door going to the Heritage Winooski Mill Museum. At Higher Ground, Violet Grohl with Suzy Clue ($20-25) plays the Showcase Lounge with doors at 7:30, and tickets are running low. Deadheads have Dead Is Alive with Dobbs' Dead ($15) at Einstein's, show at 9, and vinyl people can catch Local Dork spinning at Foam from 6 to 9. Artists can walk into the Vermont Figure Drawing Collective at Karma Bird House from 6 to 8, $20 cash, and French speakers meet for Pause-Café Mardi at Burlington Bay starting at 5. Winooski needs hands at Landry Park from 4 to 6:30, where one crew works on the mountain bike trails with Fellowship of the Wheel and another makes room for new plots in the community garden , tools, gloves and snacks provided, just show up. Early risers can join the Peace & Justice Center's Mini Clean Up Crew on the City Hall steps at 8 AM for a half hour sweep of City Hall Park, or head to Zero Gravity for the Tech Tuesdays Breakfast [MEETUP] from 8 to 10, waffles and conversation with no agenda. Over in South Burlington, the Burlington Garden Club hosts Chip Darmstadt's talk The World of Birds at Faith United Methodist Church on Dorset Street at 1, and Recreation on the Go rolls into Jaycee Park from 5:30 to 7:30 with free food, face painting, music and yard games.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday is the fullest day of the week and the last call for a couple of summer traditions. It is the final passeggiata of the season, the Italian style evening stroll up and down Church Street, anytime between 5 and 8, and downtown businesses sweeten it with deals like a free creemee with a purchase at Frankie's, a $5 glass of wine with a snack trio at Pascolo, and 20% off at ECCO. Daydream Art Supply's Summer Sketchbook Club is part of it too, from 5 to 7, bring a sketchbook and draw around the shop. The big party is Oktoberfest at American Flatbread and Mothership Brewery from 5 to 9 on the alley patio, Flatbread's 22nd and the first for Mothership, with commemorative steins, big pretzels, hot brats and polka from Inseldudler, no tickets required. And of course our own Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] runs at Pomeroy Park at 5:30, outdoors and competitive. Two shows share Higher Ground, with Grammy winner Madison Cunningham with Julia Cumming ($30-33) in the Ballroom, doors at 7:30, and Toronto soul and roots seven piece Bywater Call ($18-23) in the Showcase Lounge, a seated show with doors at 7. In Shelburne, Vermont songwriter Henry Jamison with Isabel Pless ($22) plays the Silo Sessions at Bread & Butter Farm at 7, doors at 6 with made to order tacos until showtime, the Meatpackers play the donut porch at Shelburne Orchards from 12:30 to 1:30, and Shelburne Vineyard hosts the last Wednesday Wine Down Farmers Market of the season from 5 to 9. Readers can settle in at the Silent Book Club at Bar Renée from 6 to 8, bring any book, read quietly for an hour in the middle and chat on either end. History people have Meanwhile in Vermont in the Howe Library atrium at UVM from 3 to 4:30, a panel on where Vermont shows up in the nation's founding documents, given that Vermont did not exist yet when the Declaration was signed. The Architecture + Design Film Series opens its 14th season at Contois Auditorium in City Hall with Ada, My Mother the Architect, doors at 6 and screening at 6:30, free. Digital artists can learn Blender at the Media Factory's free two part Intro to 3D Modeling workshop from 6 to 8, preregister, Mad River Distillers joins trivia night at Citizen Cider at 6:30, and Jazz Night with Ray Vega fills Hotel Vermont from 8:30 to 10:30. The Vermont Council on World Affairs holds its State of the World Summit ($75) at Hula Lakeside from 8:15 to 2:30 with Major General Henry Harder, national security correspondent J.J. Green and four time Olympian Lowell Bailey, but registration closes today, so move fast. And finally, Sunset Watchers Club teased what might be their last pop up DJ set near the Waterfront by the Frame, Wednesday night starting at 6pm. If you haven’t checked them out this summer, now might be your last chance to do so!

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday is a theater night. All Things Equal , Rupert Holmes' one woman play about Ruth Bader Ginsburg starring Michelle Azar, lands on the Flynn Main Stage at 7, and Vermont Stage opens its 32nd season with Dakar 2000 ($34-54) at Main Street Landing at 7:30, Rajiv Joseph's thriller about a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal and the government operative who asks him for a dangerous favor. Summit speaker J.J. Green sticks around town for a free conversation with Champlain College President Alex Hernandez at Fletcher Free Library from 6:30 to 8 about his book The Noise War, registration required. Comedy fans get Juno winner Sophie Buddle ($25) at Vermont Comedy Club at 7, the first of four shows through Saturday, and indie rock lifers get Luna with Constant Smiles ($30-35) in the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge, doors at 7 and tickets running low. South Burlington's Park Hop Brews sets up at Goose Pond from 5:30 to 7:30 with music from Jacob Green, food from Tejas Tex & Mex and a free yoga class at 5, and the South Burlington Public Art Gallery hosts a free opening reception for Katie Loesel's Recorded Geology from 5 to 6:30, meet the artist with light refreshments. Burlington Parks wants your ideas for a new playground and the park's comprehensive plan at a drop in session at Baird Park from 3 to 6, snacks included. UVM Health's free Health Equity Summit runs Thursday and Friday at the Davis Center with a keynote from Flint pediatrician Dr. Mona Hanna, registration required. Book clubs split two ways, with the Solarpunk Book Club & Game Night at the Peace & Justice Center from 5:30 to 6:30, free, and the Queer/LGBTQ+ Horror Book Club upstairs at the Hunny Hive on Church Street from 5:30 to 7, also free. Game people can play Blood on the Clocktower [MEETUP] at the Boardroom from 6 to 9. Catamount also runs its Social Thursday guided ride at 6 for riders comfortable on intermediate trails. Looking ahead to Saturday, our BTown Brief meetup Fall Potluck [MEETUP] at the Indian Brook pavilion in Essex is capped at 29 people, so RSVP now if you want in.
